beginner_suitability.answer: Yes. The guide is designed to be usable by lecturers with little or no previous AI experience. No programming or prompt-engineering background is required. The lecturer brings the academic expertise; the guide teaches how to provide the right material, state the task clearly, inspect the working output, correct weaknesses and save successful workflows for reuse.

responsible_use.answer: AI can assist with working material, organisation, drafting, comparison and correction, but academic accuracy, evidence, privacy, final marks, research conclusions, source validity, misconduct decisions and final academic judgement remain with the lecturer.

approved_intents.answer: The University Lecturer Edition is a 700+ page practical digital guide with 15 chapters across seven Parts, 90+ guided Prompt-Templates, practical demonstrations, checklists, worksheets, decision tools, 63 Toolkit prompts across 12 categories, interactive navigation and a Personal Lecturer AI System framework.

Yes. It is suitable for beginners. You do not need to be a programmer or prompt specialist. The guide starts from the academic work you already understand and teaches how to give AI the right material, state what you need, review the result, correct weaknesses and save what works.

The guide focuses on turning suitable recurring academic tasks into structured, reusable workflows. Instead of repeatedly starting from zero, you can work from real material, use a controlled instruction, check the working result and save successful methods for reuse. No fixed number of hours is promised.

The 90+ guided Prompt-Templates are placed beside the methods and demonstrations they support. They reduce the need to work out every recurring AI instruction from scratch and show what information to provide, what output to request and what the lecturer still needs to check.

LECTURERS'S AI TOOLKITS contains 63 definitive prompts across 12 demand-based categories. For a recurring task, find the relevant prompt, replace the required details, submit it, review the result, approve what is useful and reuse the workflow.
